keyPhrases.text: less a musical than a two-and-a-half-hour theme park ride with songs, offering as much sensory overload
I had crafted makeshift earplugs out of tissue paper
memorable mostly for the affable banality of their lyrics
Hugh Coles steals a scene or two
pretty much relegated to reproducing shtick

reasoning: Harsh criticism dominates despite acknowledging some performer qualities. Reviewer physically needed earplugs, calls it 'sensory overload,' criticizes 'banal' lyrics, and frames it as theme park entertainment rather than legitimate theater. The few positive comments about individual performers are overwhelmed by systematic critique of the production's fundamental approach.
